notes: Canonical task graph. Edit only through a deliberate plan change; state lives in state.json.

tasks.title: Bootstrap the agent harness
tasks.why: An agent with no chat history must be able to find the plan, resume, and checkpoint without a server.
steps: Verify the harness files exist and are tracked.
Run doctor, status, and next --card.
Commit the harness if it is still untracked.
tasks.done: doctor exits 0 (warnings allowed) and next returns the first ready task.
tasks.notes: The planner delivered the files; this task validates them and makes the baseline commit.

tasks.title: Add dev tooling and test entry points
tasks.why: Every later task needs a reproducible way to run tests and lint without touching the generated repo's runtime.
steps: Create pyproject.toml with project metadata and a [project.optional-dependencies] dev extra: pytest, cookiecutter, pyyaml, cffconvert, jsonschema, ruff.
Configure pytest (testpaths=tests) and ruff (line length, target py310); do not add runtime dependencies for generated repos.
Add a root Makefile with setup, test, lint, and doctor targets; setup installs the dev extra.
Add .editorconfig, .gitattributes (* text=auto eol=lf, *.pdf/*.docx binary), and docs/dev-setup.md.
Add tests/test_smoke.py so pytest has at least one test before the render helper exists.
Run make setup, then make test; if the environment has no pip/uv, block with the missing tool instead of skipping tests.
If python3 -m pip and uv are both missing, try python3 -m ensurepip --user; if that fails, block with the exact OS package command instead of installing ad hoc.

verify.cmd: python3 -c "import pathlib; assert pathlib.Path('pyproject.toml').is_file(); assert pathlib.Path('.editorconfig').is_file(); assert pathlib.Path('tests/test_smoke.py').is_file()"

tasks.done: make setup and make test pass; no runtime dep was added to the template.

tasks.title: Render helper and regression fixtures
tasks.why: Phase 1 must be driven by failing tests, not by manual inspection of rendered output.
steps: Add tests/conftest.py with a render(context, tmp_path) helper that calls cookiecutter.main.cookiecutter(no_input=True, output_dir=..., extra_context=...).
Add fixtures for: the default context; a title with &, %, _, quotes and unicode; an abstract with %, &, #; a DOI set; and an empty subtitle.
Add tests/test_render.py that renders each fixture and asserts the expected files exist.
Add xfail(strict=False) regression tests for the known defects: unparseable YAML/JSON/CFF, raw LaTeX specials, validator false positives, metadata drift.
Keep the helper tolerant of the post-gen hook creating a nested git repo in tmp_path.
tasks.done: The render matrix passes; at least one known defect is reproduced as xfail and named after the bug.
tasks.notes: Activate the venv (or use its python) before running verify, because agentctl shells out to python3.

tasks.title: Template test CI skeleton
tasks.why: A local-only harness cannot catch environment drift; CI must run the same render matrix.
steps: Add test-template.yml with permissions: contents: read and jobs: lint, unit, render.
lint runs ruff and, when present, shellcheck/yamllint; unit runs pytest; render renders the default and special-character fixtures.
In the render job, run make validate and make metadata, then git diff --exit-code to expose drift.
Pin actions to major versions now; T32 will pin SHAs. Do not add MCP or a PDF build yet.
tasks.done: The workflow is valid YAML and its render job exercises the same helper as local tests.

tasks.title: Escape structured metadata with tojson
tasks.why: Free text interpolated into YAML/JSON/CFF can make the generated repo unparseable.
steps: Replace quoted Jinja interpolation in YAML/JSON/CFF with a JSON string literal: title: {{ cookiecutter.title | tojson }} (no surrounding quotes).
Do the same for subtitle, author fields, abstract, keywords, license, DOI and any other free text in those files.
Leave README prose alone for now; its metadata/masthead block moves to a generated sentinel in T06/T10.
Add tests/test_escaping.py that renders the hostile-title fixture and yaml.safe_load/json.loads every generated file.
tasks.done: Hostile titles produce parseable YAML, JSON and CFF; the original xfail for this bug is now xpass or removed.

tasks.title: Make the abstract and keywords single-source
tasks.why: The abstract currently exists only as LaTeX, so make metadata cannot update it and metadata.yaml cannot describe the paper.
steps: Add abstract and abstract_note to metadata.yaml; store keywords as a YAML list or a documented comma-separated string.
Replace the body of 00_abstract.tex with % ABSTRACT:START/END sentinels and a placeholder body; the generator owns the content between them.
Add README:META:START/END, BACKMATTER:VERSION:START/END and CHANGES:CURRENT:START/END sentinels so later drift checks have stable targets.
Extend generate-metadata.py to write the abstract (LaTeX-escaped), keywords, README masthead and CHANGES current-release block from metadata.yaml, leaving files untouched when already correct.
Add tests that mutate metadata.yaml and check the sentinels update without duplicating content.
tasks.done: The abstract and keywords are read from metadata.yaml; LaTeX, README and CHANGES blocks are generated between stable sentinels.

tasks.title: Drive PDF metadata from the title block
tasks.why: make metadata must update PDF title/author/subject/keywords, not just the visible title.
steps: Extend the METADATA:TITLE_BLOCK generated region to include \hypersetup{pdftitle=...,pdfauthor=...,pdfsubject=...,pdfkeywords=...}.
Alternatively use \hypersetup{pdfusetitle} plus a generated \paperKeywords; choose one and document it.
Keep the visible title/author block working and do not introduce a second source of truth.
Add a text-level test that checks the generated block contains the expected escaped values for the hostile-title fixture.
tasks.done: make metadata rewrites PDF metadata in article.tex; a text test covers special characters and an empty subtitle.

tasks.title: Fix latex_escape and add property tests
tasks.why: The current escape order can double-escape backslashes and miss characters that break compilation.
steps: Implement latex_escape(text, already_tex=False) with a single-pass mapping for \ & % $ # _ { } ~ ^ and a documented unicode policy.
Never re-escape generated backslashes; support an explicit title_tex override for authors who need raw LaTeX.
Add table-driven tests covering every special character, double escaping, empty strings and unicode.
tasks.done: Every special character round-trips through the escaper; idempotence is tested.

tasks.title: Run the metadata generator after rendering
tasks.why: A fresh render must already be coherent; relying on the user to run make metadata leaves the repo inconsistent.
steps: In post_gen_project.py, run the generated scripts/generate-metadata.py with sys.executable and cwd=the generated project.
Fail with a clear message if PyYAML is missing; do not silently skip generation.
Add an idempotency test: render, snapshot, run make metadata, assert git diff is empty, for default, DOI-set and hostile-input fixtures.
Make the hook safe to run twice.
tasks.done: A fresh render is byte-identical after make metadata in all fixtures, including DOI set.

tasks.title: Add metadata --check and wire it into CI
tasks.why: Without a drift check, generated artifacts silently diverge from metadata.yaml.
steps: Add --check to generate-metadata.py: compute expected content, compare with disk, print a unified diff and exit 1 on drift.
Add make metadata-check and make metadata (write) as separate targets; make pdf must not depend on a write.
Run metadata-check in the template CI render job.
Add tests for clean, drifted and missing-file cases.
tasks.done: make metadata-check fails on drift and succeeds on a fresh render; CI runs it.
tasks.notes: Gate G1 after this task: run make test, audit, and render STATUS.md.

tasks.title: Rewrite CFF generation
tasks.why: The current CITATION.cff is invalid: type manuscript is not allowed, version loads as a float, and free text is unescaped.
steps: Generate CFF with yaml.safe_dump(sort_keys=False, allow_unicode=True); never hand-format YAML.
Use root type: software and a valid preferred-citation (generic for an unpublished manuscript, or article only when a journal is known).
Quote version and date-released so version stays a string; include abstract, keywords, identifiers and authors from metadata.
Omit empty optional fields rather than emitting null/empty strings.
Add tests that parse the CFF with PyYAML and assert field types; run cffconvert --validate when available.
tasks.done: CITATION.cff parses, has valid types, and keeps version as a string.

tasks.title: Rewrite Zenodo deposit generation
tasks.why: The current .zenodo.json has invalid communities, a license id Zenodo does not use, and fragile creator/orcid shapes.
steps: Generate JSON with json.dumps; map SPDX ids to Zenodo vocabulary ids (CC-BY-4.0 -> cc-by-4.0).
Default communities to [] unless a valid, verified community id is configured; never invent one.
Set publication_type explicitly (preprint/article) and omit empty doi, orcid, related_identifiers.
Model creators as a list of {name, orcid?, affiliation?} entries.
Add tests for default, DOI set, multi-creator and license variants.
tasks.done: The deposit JSON is valid, uses the Zenodo license vocabulary, and has no unverified communities.

tasks.title: Schema validation tests and CI
tasks.why: Parsing is not validity; CFF and Zenodo have schemas that catch semantic mistakes.
steps: Add offline schema/type assertions for CFF and Zenodo output.
Add a network-marked test (RUN_NETWORK=1) that resolves Zenodo community/license ids and validates CFF with cffconvert.
Add a non-blocking CI job for the network checks; the default test run must stay offline and green.
tasks.done: Offline tests pass; network tests skip cleanly and run in the non-blocking job.
tasks.notes: Network tests must never gate make test, make pdf, or pre-push.

tasks.title: Honor the selected license
tasks.why: The LICENSE file currently ignores cookiecutter.license, which is a legal correctness bug.
steps: Restrict the license choice to CC-BY-4.0 (default), CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0, and MIT, with human prompts.
Vendor the full text of each license under licenses/ and have the post-gen hook copy the selected one to LICENSE.
Add a code_license choice (default MIT) and emit LICENSE-CODE when it differs from the paper license.
Link the selected license and code license from README and record the SPDX id in metadata.yaml.
Add a render-matrix test asserting the LICENSE text matches the choice for every option.
tasks.done: Every license choice yields the correct full text and README link; unknown licenses fail at pre-gen.

tasks.title: Rewrite validator comment/cite/input handling
tasks.why: The validator misses commented text and cite keys and produces false positives for inline input.
steps: Strip comments with a multiline-aware pattern and respect escaped percent signs.
Check \citep, \citet, \citealp, \citeauthor, \citeyear and \nocite keys, including comma-separated lists.
Handle inline \input{...}/\include{...} and ignore occurrences inside comments.
Emit structured diagnostics (file, line, code, message) while preserving the existing CLI and exit behavior.
Add fixtures for every historical false positive/negative.
tasks.done: Every fixture from the review has a test; no commented text is treated as live input.

tasks.title: Add structural validator checks
tasks.why: The current validator checks only a fraction of what breaks a submission.
steps: Check \includegraphics paths against \graphicspath and the filesystem.
Check \ref targets exist, labels are unique, and unused labels are reported as warnings.
Check bib keys against refs.bib, duplicate keys, and orphan entries.
Check that includes cannot escape the paper directory; recurse with a depth limit.
Keep warnings separate from errors so CI can choose strictness.
tasks.done: Structural fixtures cover missing figures, broken refs, duplicate labels and orphan bib entries.

tasks.title: Make CI call the one validator
tasks.why: CI currently duplicates validator logic, so CI and make validate can disagree.
steps: Replace inline Python/shell validation in the workflow with python3 scripts/validate-paper.py.
Run the same command in make validate; do not duplicate flags.
Add permissions: contents: read, concurrency, and path filters that match the generated repo layout.
Add a test that renders a repo and asserts make validate and the workflow use the same entry point.
tasks.done: There is exactly one validator implementation; CI and make validate invoke it identically.

tasks.title: Fix git init and pre-push hook installation
tasks.why: Running cookiecutter inside a git repo skips git init and silently fails to install the pre-push hook.
steps: Compare the generated path with git rev-parse --show-toplevel; only git init when the generated repo is not already inside one.
Install the hook with git config core.hooksPath or by copying it to .git/hooks; make hooks must be idempotent.
Never fail the render when git is missing; print an actionable warning instead.
Add an integration test that renders inside a temporary git repo and asserts the hook is installed once.
tasks.done: Nested renders no longer create a broken repo; the hook is installed once and make hooks is safe to rerun.

tasks.title: Harden the bootstrap workflow
tasks.why: User-supplied workflow inputs are interpolated into shell, which is a command-injection risk.
steps: Pass inputs through env: variables and quote every expansion; never interpolate ${{ inputs.* }} directly inside run:.
Validate topic against a slug regex, repo_name against the expected pattern, and version against semver before use.
Use cookiecutter --no-input with an explicit context; make repository creation idempotent and set topics/permissions explicitly.
Add a test that parses the workflow YAML and fails if a run block contains ${{ inputs. or ${{ github.event.inputs.
tasks.done: No workflow input reaches a shell unquoted; invalid inputs fail before any git/GitHub command runs.

tasks.title: Make DOCX respect graphics paths and references
tasks.why: Pandoc does not read LaTeX \graphicspath, so figures silently disappear from DOCX.
steps: Add --resource-path for paper, paper/figures and the repo root to the pandoc command.
Support an optional reference.docx and a documented template path.
Use pandoc/core or a pinned pandoc version in CI; keep local behavior identical.
Add a test that renders a repo with a figure in paper/figures and inspects the DOCX zip for the image (skip if pandoc is absent).
Document and optionally downscale oversized figures for DOCX; do not silently alter the PDF source images.
tasks.done: DOCX includes figures from \graphicspath and CI uses the same command as make docx.

tasks.title: Extract the vendored core library
tasks.why: Validator, generator, hooks, CI and a future MCP adapter must share one implementation.
steps: Create scripts/article/ as a stdlib-only package: __init__.py, core.py, metadata.py, latex.py, validate.py, build.py, diagnostics.py.
Move pure logic out of validate-paper.py and generate-metadata.py; no printing, no process exit, no cwd assumptions.
Represent diagnostics, metadata and build plans as dataclasses or plain dicts with stable keys.
Add JSON schemas under schemas/ for diagnostics and status.
Keep imports working in Python 3.10 and in a generated repo with only stdlib + PyYAML.
tasks.done: Core functions are pure, unit-tested, and importable without side effects or third-party deps beyond PyYAML.

tasks.title: Add the JSON-first CLI
tasks.why: Make, hooks, CI and MCP need one machine-readable entry point with stable exit codes.
steps: Implement python3 -m scripts.article with subcommands: validate, metadata, status, build, release (release may be a stub until T33).
Every command supports --json and returns 0 ok, 1 diagnostics/failure, 2 usage, 3 internal.
Add --check/--dry-run where a command can mutate files; stdout stays machine-readable, logs go to stderr.
Do not import or call any MCP code.
Test each command via a rendered fixture, including exit codes and JSON schema validation.
tasks.done: CLI subcommands are documented by --help, emit stable JSON, and use the agreed exit codes.

tasks.title: Delegate Make, hooks and CI to the CLI
tasks.why: Keeping shell copies of the logic defeats the single-source-of-truth design.
steps: make pdf/validate/metadata/metadata-check/docx call the CLI (or keep file targets but share the core).
pre-push calls the CLI and remains safe when the CLI is missing (warn, do not break unrelated pushes).
Turn validate-paper.py and generate-metadata.py into thin deprecated shims that parse the old flags and delegate.
Preserve byte-identical output for existing commands.
Add a test that every entry point produces the same diagnostics for the same fixture.
tasks.done: No business logic remains in Make/hooks/CI/shims; old entry points still work.

tasks.title: Add article status and publish the JSON contract
tasks.why: Agents and humans need one command that says what is true about the repo without parsing logs.
steps: Implement article status [--json] with template_version, metadata validity, metadata drift, diagnostics summary, tool versions and dirty-tree state.
Write schemas/status.schema.json and validate the output against it in tests.
Document the exit codes and JSON fields in docs/cli.md; state that the contract is versioned with the template.
Keep status read-only and offline.
tasks.done: status is schema-valid, offline and read-only; docs match the implementation.

tasks.title: Add the v2 authors/affiliations loader
tasks.why: A single author_name field cannot represent real papers, and v2 is the agreed schema break.
steps: Add authors: as a list of mappings (name, given, family, orcid, affiliations, corresponding, email, ror) and affiliations: as an id->mapping map.
Normalize the legacy author_name/author_orcid/author_affiliation fields with a deprecation warning; do not break v1 repos.
Validate ORCID checksums, duplicate affiliations and missing corresponding authors.
Record metadata_schema: 2 in the new schema while still reading v1.
Add fixtures for legacy, multi-author, mononym, and invalid ORCID.
Accept ROR ids on affiliations and validate their shape (https://ror.org/...); do not require them.
tasks.done: Both schema versions load; invalid author/affiliation data (including malformed ORCID/ROR) produces actionable diagnostics.

tasks.title: Render multiple authors everywhere
tasks.why: Authors must be consistent across LaTeX, CFF, Zenodo and README.
steps: Render authors with authblk or explicit \author/\thanks blocks, including affiliations and corresponding markers.
Generate CFF authors, Zenodo creators and README author lines from the same normalized model.
Render ORCID and ROR as links where the medium supports it; omit them where empty.
Add a test that asserts all four outputs agree for a 3-author fixture.
tasks.done: A multi-author fixture is consistent across LaTeX/CFF/Zenodo/README and builds when latexmk is available.

tasks.title: Parameterize manuscript kind and citation style
tasks.why: The template is currently hard-wired to a perspective essay with one bibliography style.
steps: Add manuscript_kind choices (perspective default, empirical, review) and citation_style choices (author-year, numeric).
Conditionally include the methods/results sections and required packages; keep the perspective output unchanged by default.
Select the bibliography style from citation_style and pass the same choice to DOCX/HTML.
Add a render matrix test over kind x style, asserting expected sections/packages and no LaTeX errors in the static check.
tasks.done: Every kind/style combination renders; the default is byte-identical to the current perspective output.

tasks.title: Add pre-gen validation and human prompts
tasks.why: Bad slugs, versions or ORCIDs should fail before a half-written repo exists.
steps: Validate topic/repo_name slug rules, semver, ORCID checksum, license, DOI shape and non-empty title.
Add __prompts__ with plain-language labels; keep --no-input working for CI.
Fail with one actionable message per invalid field, not a traceback.
Test valid and invalid contexts through cookiecutter's API.
tasks.done: Invalid contexts fail before rendering; prompts are human-readable and CI still runs --no-input.

tasks.title: Make workflows branch-agnostic
tasks.why: Hard-coded master filters break new repos that use main.
steps: Remove branches: [master] filters or replace them with the repository default branch; use github.event.repository.default_branch where needed.
Push HEAD rather than a hard-coded branch name.
Add an optional default_branch choice and document it.
Add a test that parses the workflows and fails on a literal master/main branch filter.
tasks.done: No workflow assumes master; a main-based repo passes the same jobs.

tasks.title: Fix the preamble and make builds out-of-tree
tasks.why: Package order and in-tree builds cause fragile, noisy repos and non-reproducible artifacts.
steps: Load titlesec before hyperref (or remove it); load cleveref after hyperref; keep pdfusetitle consistent with T07.
Review the package list: load csquotes and siunitx only when used; keep hyperref late and cleveref after it.
Add .latexmkrc with -outdir=build, -halt-on-error, -file-line-error and a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH for reproducible runs.
Make clean remove build artifacts; make pdf must work from a fresh clone.
Add static tests for package order and for the expected build directory.
tasks.done: A clean build produces build/article.pdf, leaves no aux files in the source tree, and the preamble order is documented.

tasks.title: Repo hygiene, docs and neutral defaults
tasks.why: Stale README trees, personal defaults and a jinja2-time dependency make the template harder to use.
steps: Remove the jinja2_time extension: set date to a placeholder and fill it with the stdlib in post_gen, or document a safe default.
Refresh .gitignore for build/, .venv, __pycache__, .DS_Store, LaTeX aux files, paper/figures/generated/, paper/supplementary/build/ and biblatex intermediates.
Rewrite the README tree/prerequisites/license sections to match actual behavior; add CONTRIBUTING.md.
Document how to override personal defaults without editing tracked files.
Add doc tests that grep for stale paths and commands.
Add a small, accurate badge block (CI, license, template version) only for services the repo actually uses.
tasks.done: Docs describe the actual tree and commands; the template has no undeclared Jinja extension.

tasks.title: Harden CI: reusable build, permissions, pinning
tasks.why: Duplicated CI logic and floating actions are both a maintenance and supply-chain risk.
steps: Extract a reusable build workflow used by test-template and the generated repo's CI.
Set least-privilege permissions, concurrency groups and a tag/release guard.
Pin third-party actions to commit SHAs with version comments; pin the TeX Live action and enable caching.
Add Dependabot for actions and pip.
Add a test that parses every workflow and asserts permissions are present and no unpinned uses: remains.
tasks.done: All workflows parse, use least privilege, and have no floating third-party actions.

tasks.title: Add release plan/apply and DOI handling
tasks.why: Releases are currently manual and DOI metadata drifts from the tag; apply must stay offline and reviewable.
steps: Implement release plan --json: version, tag, doi, artifact list, checks, and a dry-run diff.
Implement release apply only with an explicit --yes; require a clean tree, an absent tag, and a version bump.
Set the DOI in metadata.yaml and regenerate every derived file; never edit generated files directly.
Add tests for clean/dirty trees, existing tags, invalid versions and DOI assignment.
Do not call the Zenodo API from release apply; emit the deposit payload (or print the command) and leave network upload to an explicit, separate step.
tasks.done: release plan is read-only and schema-valid; release apply is gated, deterministic and idempotent.

tasks.title: Add diff, arXiv, wordcount, spell, watch and figures
tasks.why: These are the remaining daily authoring tasks that still require memorizing tool flags.
steps: Add make diff (latexdiff between two refs), arxiv (flatten and sanitize), wordcount, spell, watch and figures.
Each target must fail with an actionable message when its external tool is missing; no silent success.
arxiv must not include build artifacts, .git, or private notes; test the file list.
Keep all of these out of make pdf and CI gates unless explicitly invoked.
tasks.done: Each target has a unit test for its command construction and a clear missing-tool message.

tasks.title: Reproducible builds, Pages and supplementary
tasks.why: Archival deposits need verifiable builds and a stable public artifact.
steps: Build twice with a fixed SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH and compare PDF hashes; document any allowed variance.
Add a Pages job that deploys build/article.pdf (and supplementary) from a tag.
Add a supplementary build target and artifact retention.
Test the workflow wiring and the double-build script; skip the real build when latexmk is absent.
tasks.done: Two clean builds match, Pages deploys only from a tag, and supplementary artifacts are attached.

tasks.title: Add article migrate for v1 repos
tasks.why: The v2 schema break is only acceptable if existing repos have a safe upgrade path.
steps: Detect v1 metadata, write a backup, map author/license/version fields to v2, and regenerate derived files.
Support --dry-run and --check; never overwrite without a backup or --yes.
Document manual review points (multi-author splitting, affiliations, ORCID).
Test a legacy fixture end-to-end and assert idempotence.
tasks.done: A v1 fixture migrates with a backup, passes validation, and a second run is a no-op.

tasks.title: Data and analysis pipeline (optional)
tasks.why: Empirical manuscripts need a reproducible path from data to figures/tables.
steps: Add opt-in data/ and analysis/ directories with a lockfile (uv or renv) and checksums.
Add make analysis that regenerates figures/tables into paper/figures and paper/tables.
Do not run analysis in make pdf unless the user opts in; fail clearly when the env is missing.
Test the pipeline with a tiny fixture dataset.
tasks.done: make analysis is reproducible from a clean checkout and its outputs are gitignored or checked intentionally.

tasks.title: Journal class adapters (optional)
tasks.why: Submission targets have different class files and front matter; guessing is worse than an explicit adapter.
steps: Add optional journal choices (elsarticle, acmart, IEEEtran) without making any of them the default.
Provide vendored classes/templates only when their licenses allow it; otherwise document installation.
Add a submission checklist per journal.
Test the render matrix; skip PDF builds when the class is unavailable.
tasks.done: Every adapter renders and documents its requirements; the default perspective output is unchanged.

tasks.title: Reviewer mode and response letters (optional)
tasks.why: Revision workflows are common and easy to standardize.
steps: Add a review_mode choice that enables line numbers, anonymization and a changed-text marker.
Add response-letter and cover-letter templates with generated metadata.
Ensure anonymous mode removes authors, acknowledgements and identifying links.
Test both modes for leaked identity fields.
tasks.done: Anonymous mode leaks no identity; review mode builds and is documented.

tasks.title: Devcontainer (optional)
tasks.why: A pinned environment removes the 'works on my machine' TeX/Pandoc problem.
steps: Create a devcontainer with TeX Live, pandoc, Python 3.10+, git and the dev extras.
Pin image digests and document the build; do not make it required for local builds.
Add VS Code tasks for make pdf/validate/test.
Add a static test for the config; the real docker build stays opt-in.
tasks.done: The devcontainer config is valid and documented; normal builds do not depend on Docker.

tasks.title: REUSE/SPDX compliance (optional)
tasks.why: Per-file licensing is needed if the template is shared publicly.
steps: Add SPDX headers or a REUSE.toml mapping for template files, scripts and paper content.
Vendor license texts under LICENSES/ and keep them in sync with T14.
Add an opt-in reuse lint target; do not gate the default build on the reuse tool.
Test that every tracked file is covered by a mapping or header.
tasks.done: Every tracked file has a license mapping; reuse lint passes when the tool is installed.

tasks.title: Template upgrade path (optional)
tasks.why: Generated repos need a supported way to pick up template fixes without losing local edits.
steps: Evaluate cruft vs Copier against the constraint that generated repos stay archival.
Stamp template_version and a minimal template context into the generated repo.
Document a three-way-merge upgrade and a manual fallback; never auto-merge.
Test that the stamp is written and that upgrade instructions match actual files.
tasks.done: A generated repo records its template version and has a tested upgrade procedure.

tasks.title: Read-only MCP adapter (optional)
tasks.why: Agents can consume the CLI contract without making MCP part of the build.
steps: Create a separate optional package under mcp/ that imports the core or shells out to the CLI --json; never the inverse.
Expose read-only tools/resources: validate, status, metadata plan, diagnostics, file reads limited to the repo.
Add path allowlisting, output size limits and no secret/env leakage.
Test parity between the MCP output and the CLI JSON for the same fixture.
tasks.done: MCP is installable as an extra, read-only by default, and byte-parity with CLI JSON.

tasks.title: MCP mutating tools with confirmation (optional)
tasks.why: Write operations are useful but dangerous; they need an explicit plan/confirm protocol.
steps: Add plan/confirm tokens for metadata writes, release apply and migrate; tokens expire and are single-use.
Refuse writes outside the repo, enforce timeouts, and append an audit log.
Never expose network or shell passthrough.
Test refusal paths: stale token, path escape, missing confirmation.
tasks.done: Every mutation requires a fresh confirmation and is confined to the repo.
